subject: Token flow interruption — timeline, impact, action items
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@nebulaai.com>, ops@nebulaai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Token flow interruption — timeline, impact, action items

Hi Sarah / Nebula ops team,

We observed a token-flow interruption impacting your reserved GPU pool between 08:05 and 09:02 PST this morning. Early indicators: 30–40% increased 5xx responses for generation routes and elevated queue latency on the dedicated pool serving your account.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm which customers/apps were most affected on your side? (service IDs or example request IDs are helpful)
- Do you want us to proceed with a public-facing incident note to your engineering Slack channel?

What we’re doing now:
1) Ops are preserving kernel/metrics snapshots and we’ve captured the scheduler profiles (attached timeline CSV and a Grafana screenshot).
2) Karthik is triaging autoscaler and allocator logs to identify if this was an autoscale lag or a kernel-level eviction.
3) We’re staging a temporary routing rule to shift a subset (~10%) of traffic to a warm standby pool to reduce immediate latency.

Attachments: token_flow_timeline.csv, grafana_screenshot.png

I’ll follow up with a clearer timeline and remediation plan within the next 6 hours. Apologies for the disruption; we know how sensitive this is for your SLAs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@nebulaai.com>

Subject: Re: Token flow interruption — timeline, impact, action items

Ben — thanks for the heads up.

Impact from our side: our customer-facing inference endpoint (prod-infer-1) returned 502/503 for approx 7k requests during the window you mentioned; several partner integrations timed out. I pulled a few request IDs and attached a short error log (customer_impact_log.pdf).

We appreciate keeping this tight and public comms are fine — please send a note to our eng Slack (#nebula-ops) and CC me. Regarding credits: our renewal rep will expect a remediation plan + credit path if total successful tokens fall below our expected baseline.

For now: we need ETA for the routing change and an interim mitigation that prevents repeated bursts while you investigate root cause.

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Engineering | Nebula AI
sarah@nebulaai.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:30:18 -0800
Subject: RE: Token flow interruption — timeline, impact, action items

Ben / Marissa — quick triage summary:

Preliminary root cause (high confidence): a cgroup memory accounting leak in our GPU allocator led to an internal watcher triggering conservative eviction of warm workers. That caused sustained queue starvation for tenants pinned to the affected nodes; autoscaler activity lagged due to an edge-case in the warmup backoff logic.

Why it became customer-visible: Nebula AI’s workload has a tight token-per-second profile with many long-context calls. When the warm workers were evicted, the transition to cold starts plus autoscaler backoff created the error spike you saw.

Short-term mitigations we recommend (today):
- Apply the temporary routing rule Ben proposed to steer 12% of traffic to the warm-standby pool (reduces cold-start tail).
- Disable warmup backoff for Nebula's reservation for the next 24 hours.
- Increase per-tenant concurrency cap by +20% to reduce per-request queuing.

Planned fixes:
- Patch allocator to fix cgroup accounting and deploy canary tonight (RED-3821).
- Adjust autoscaler warmup backoff algorithm to avoid stuck states when warm workers are briefly evicted.

Customer credit guidance: recommend offering Nebula a 10% service credit for the impacted monthly usage plus a goodwill credit to cover partner escalations. Ops will prepare the exact numbers once we reconcile token counts.

I attached a short screenshot of allocator metrics (grafana_screenshot.png) and a CSV timeline (token_flow_timeline.csv).

Karthik
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 15:23:41 -0800
Subject: RE: Token flow interruption — timeline, impact, action items

Sarah / Nebula ops — follow-up and next steps.

Thanks for the quick details and the log; that helped us speed up the triage. Below is the consolidated timeline and the concrete actions we’re committing to.

Incident timeline (consolidated):
- 08:04 PST: first anomalous allocator eviction event detected (warm workers).
- 08:05–08:35 PST: progressive queue latency increase and elevated 5xx for generation routes.
- 08:36 PST: our automated mitigation attempted to spin additional nodes but backoff prevented fast ramp — error window widened.
- 08:58 PST: temporary routing rule engaged, 12% traffic shifted to warm standby — immediate latency drop observed.
- 09:02 PST: error rates returned to baseline; we continued elevated monitoring through 12:00 PST.

What we did for you:
- Engaged warm-standby routing (12% of traffic) and disabled warmup backoff for Nebula reservation for 24 hrs.
- Captured full allocator and autoscaler logs and preserved relevant kernels for postmortem.
- Opened Jira RED-3821 for the allocator fix; canary deploy targeted tonight.

Committed deliverables & timeline:
- 48-hour interim report: root cause write-up + token reconciliation (by 2026-12-09 17:00 PST).
- Patch canary deploy for allocator accounting fix: targeted 2026-12-08 23:00 PST; full rollout after canary verification.
- Final postmortem and remediation plan: by 2026-12-15 EOD PST.

Customer credit: we propose a 10% service credit on impacted monthly usage and a $5k goodwill credit to reimburse partner escalations. Marissa from Commercial will follow up with exact numbers and credit mechanics.

Requested from you:
- Confirm you’re OK with the proposed temporary routing and the canary timing.
- Any additional request IDs or SLA impact reports you want included in the postmortem.

We’ll publish an incident note to your #nebula-ops Slack channel once you confirm.

Apologies again for the interruption — we recognize the operational pain this causes and will move fast to close the loop.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: token_flow_timeline.csv, grafana_screenshot.png, customer_impact_log.pdf
